In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
soaking after preheating and fermentation are the most effective in removing phytic acid from faba bean, but the effect on zinc bioavailability is not clear.
wet processing of faba bean, especially germination, is effective in reducing phytic acid and increasing in vitro zinc solubilization.
soaking after preheating is the best treatment to increase the in vitro zinc bioavailability of faba bean.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
soaking after dry preheated faba beans at 10°C for 24 h was the most effective in reducing phytic acid content and increasing zinc solubility.
wet fermentation and germination treatments are more effective than soaking in decreasing the levels of phytic acid, and thus increasing the availability of zinc in fababean.
the phytic acid content in faba beans was reduced by 48-84% after wet and dry processing procedures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the processing of faba beans with the expectation of increasing the bioavailability of their micronutrients is not always successful.
the phytic acid content and in vitro zinc solubilities of faba bean are significantly reduced by fermentation and soaking at 10 °C after preheating.
soaking faba bean after wet prehearing at 10°C is a promising method to increase zinc availability in faba bean.
